oil.summary: A deeply bifurcated session in crude. WTI surged +2.83% to $92.97/bbl, reflecting ongoing Hormuz risk premium after three tankers were struck by unknown projectiles in the strait and Indian refiners scrambled to secure tanker capacity. Brent, however, slipped -1.08% to $102.41 on reports that the US has temporarily eased Russia oil sanctions to cap the price surge — a move that riled European allies and introduced fresh supply-side relief. Heating oil cratered -6.35% to $4.6424/gal, the session's sharpest mover, partly tied to the diesel export-ban discussion after Trump acknowledged a potential ban could negatively impact gasoline prices. Ukraine's strikes on 45% of Russian refining capacity and the Lindsey Graham sanctions act targeting buyers of Russian energy remain structural overhangs. CME options markets price a 77% probability of an OPEC cut at the next meeting, consistent with elevated market uncertainty.
drivers: Hormuz tanker strikes and Indian refiner demand for shipping capacity support WTI's +2.83% bid
US temporary easing of Russia oil sanctions caps Brent upside and triggers a -1.08% pullback
Heating oil -6.35% on Trump's diesel export-ban commentary and potential supply-side recalibration

gas.summary: Henry Hub continued to bleed lower, falling -1.95% to $2.966/MMBtu and now down -10.01% on the week — a notable divergence from geopolitical noise driving oil. No gas-specific supply disruption headlines were present today to arrest the decline. TTF edged up +0.91% to €73.015/MWh, holding closer to flat on the month, with European markets remaining more sensitive to broader energy security concerns. Pakistan's consideration of direct spot LNG imports for power plants adds a marginal demand signal on the LNG side. The BLM opening of 35,000 California acres to an oil and gas lease sale in December points to modest future supply expansion domestically. Overall, gas headline flow today was thin and insufficient to reverse Henry Hub's downward trajectory.
drivers: Henry Hub -1.95% on the day and -10.01% on the week; no supply disruption catalyst present
TTF +0.91% holds relatively firm, reflecting lingering European energy security premium
Pakistan spot LNG import consideration provides a marginal demand-side signal for global LNG markets

power.summary: EU carbon EUAs were essentially unchanged at $81.41 (-0.23%), consolidating a +3.05% monthly gain. The power sector headlines today were dominated by nuclear themes: Amazon secured a 20-year nuclear power agreement with Constellation Energy, with a Goldman analyst calling it broadly positive for the industry under the 'Powering Up America' theme. Uranium long-term prices hit an all-time record of $96/lb, though nuclear equities sold off in a divergent signal. Commonwealth Fusion Systems inked a historic superconductor deal, advancing commercial fusion timelines. India's power shortfall hit a three-year high in September driven by El Niño conditions and rising industrial demand. Taiwan allocated $13 billion to shield consumers from elevated energy costs, supporting Taipower and refiner CPC.
drivers: Amazon-Constellation 20-year nuclear deal and record uranium prices at $96/lb underscore accelerating nuclear demand
India's power shortfall reaches three-year high in September on El Niño and industrial demand surge
Taiwan's $13 billion energy cost support package highlights government intervention as power prices remain elevated
